content.text: The document affirmatively rejects minimum commitments in two places, matching our preferred position.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Clause 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms Customer pays only for Services actually ordered, with no breach or shortfall for declining further Order Forms — our preferred position. Clause 12.3 reinforces that Customer has given no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment, and clause 7.1 bars Vendor from imposing minimum-use or similar charges not stated in an Order Form. Sections 4, 7 and 8 contain no committed spend, take-or-pay, shortfall true-up or volume cap on Customer usage; Order Forms renew only in twelve-month increments with a thirty-day non-renewal right (8.2). No redline needed for this rule. (Separately, the liquidated-damages construct in 7.7 is a late-payment penalty issue outside this rule's scope.)
